fix.shows: The Wire sets side by side the three counts of Rajasthan's electors made in 2026. The final roll of the Special Intensive Revision held 5.15 crore electors, the draft roll of the special summary revision now under way holds 5.26 crore, and the State Election Commission's final roll for the panchayat and municipal elections holds 5.45 crore. It explains that the Election Commission prepares the rolls for Lok Sabha and Assembly elections under Article 324 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950, while State Election Commissions prepare the rolls for panchayat and municipal elections under Articles 243K and 243ZA. It reports, from the Times of India, that the State Election Commission's secretary Rajesh Verma said his office built its rolls from the Commission's roll from before the revision, as last updated on 1 January 2025, because preparations for the local elections began before the revision was over. It cites a comparison by Nikhil Dey, a founder of the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, which found 26.63 lakh electors deleted in the revision still on the State Election Commission's local body rolls, and his question how people the revision found dead could be on the state's roll. It notes that the claims and objections of the summary revision may change the count again by January 2027.

fix.shows: The Times of India reports an analysis by the People's Union for Civil Liberties, dated 11 November, which found that more than 26 lakh of the 41.65 lakh electors deleted from Rajasthan's draft roll in the Special Intensive Revision are still on the State Election Commission's rolls for the 2026 panchayat and urban local body elections, 13.7 lakh on the panchayat rolls and 12.4 lakh on the municipal rolls. The analysis covers the State Election Commission's second supplement to the panchayat rolls, published up to 12 October. By PUCL's count these include 3,20,395 people the Election Commission marked dead, more than 17.32 lakh it deleted as shifted, 3.67 lakh as untraceable or absent and more than 1.83 lakh as enrolled elsewhere. Baran has the highest share of deleted electors still on the State Election Commission's rolls, 83.1%, followed by Pali, Jalore, Bikaner, Sirohi and Deedwana-Kuchaman, all above 80%. Of those marked dead, 70.7% in Banswara are still on the rolls, and PUCL says that in seven districts at least half of those marked dead are still on them. The figure is 69,343 lower than PUCL's earlier count of nearly 26.7 lakh from the panchayat rolls of 25 February, and the number marked dead and still listed fell by 31,987 from 3,52,382. PUCL puts the active names across the State Election Commission's rolls at 5,47,86,896, which is 32,72,934 or 6.4% more than the Election Commission's final roll of 5,15,13,962. The State Election Commission's secretary Rajesh Verma told the paper that the state's roll numbers have increased in recent months and that the update process likely reduced the gap.
